title: Cat Ba Island and how to get there
text: Cat Ba is the largest island of Hai Phong and the main base for visiting Lan Ha Bay. From the city, go by bus or car across the Tan Vu - Lach Huyen sea bridge to Got pier, then take the short car ferry to Cai Vieng on Cat Ba, a crossing of about 15 to 20 minutes. Cat Ba town has hotels, seafood restaurants and the small Cat Co beaches.

title: Lan Ha Bay
text: Lan Ha Bay lies south-east of Cat Ba Island and has hundreds of limestone islets, quiet lagoons and small sandy beaches. Most visitors join a day cruise from Cat Ba that includes kayaking and swimming stops. Together with Ha Long Bay, the Cat Ba archipelago was recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2023.
source: UNESCO World Heritage listing, Ha Long Bay - Cat Ba Archipelago (to verify)

title: Cat Ba National Park
text: Cat Ba National Park covers much of the island's forested interior. It is home to the Cat Ba langur, a critically endangered monkey with a golden-yellow head that lives only on this island. A popular hiking trail climbs to the Ngu Lam peak viewpoint; wear good shoes because the path is steep and rocky.
source: Cat Ba National Park information (to verify)

title: Do Son Beach
text: Do Son is a seaside peninsula about 20 km south-east of the city centre and the closest beach area to Hai Phong. The coast is divided into three zones, with hotels and seafood restaurants along the shore. The water is often brownish because of river sediment, so it is better for a seaside walk and seafood than for clear-water swimming.

title: Hai Phong Opera House
text: The Opera House is a French colonial building completed in 1912 in the centre of the city. Its cream facade, columns and the square in front of it make it the city's best-known photo spot, especially in the evening when it is lit up. Concerts and official events are still held inside.
source: Hai Phong city heritage information (to verify)

title: Du Hang Pagoda
text: Du Hang is one of the oldest pagodas in Hai Phong, first built around a thousand years ago and rebuilt several times since. It is located in Le Chan district and is known for its fine wooden carvings, a stone bridge over a small pond and a quiet garden. Visitors should dress modestly and keep their voices down.
source: Hai Phong cultural heritage information (to verify)

title: Hai Phong Museum
text: The Hai Phong Museum is housed in a red French-era building on Dien Bien Phu street in the city centre. Its exhibits cover the history of the port city, the Bach Dang river battles and local culture. It is a good indoor stop on a hot or rainy afternoon.

title: Banh da cua (crab noodle soup)
text: Banh da cua is the signature dish of Hai Phong: wide, flat red-brown rice noodles in a broth made from small field crabs, topped with crab paste, fried tofu, water spinach and sometimes pork rolls. It is usually eaten for breakfast or lunch at small local shops all over the city.

title: Banh mi que (stick bread)
text: Banh mi que is a long, thin, crispy baguette filled with pate and a spicy chili sauce. It costs only a few thousand dong per stick, so people often order several at once. It is a typical Hai Phong street snack, found at small stalls in the evening.

title: Nem cua be (square crab spring rolls)
text: Nem cua be are square-shaped fried spring rolls filled with sea crab meat, pork, mushrooms and glass noodles. They are crispy outside and are eaten with fresh herbs, rice noodles and a sweet and sour dipping sauce. Many seafood restaurants in the city serve them.

title: Red flamboyant flower season
text: Hai Phong is called the city of red flamboyant flowers (hoa phuong do). The trees along the main streets bloom bright red mainly in May and June, and the city holds its Red Flamboyant Flower Festival in that period. This is a good time for photos in the city centre.

title: Best time to visit
text: Hai Phong has four seasons. Late spring (April to early June) and autumn (September to November) are the most pleasant times. Summer from June to August is hot and good for beaches and Cat Ba, but storms can stop boats and ferries. Winter from December to February is cool and often grey.

title: Getting from Hanoi to Hai Phong
text: Hai Phong is about 100 km east of Hanoi. The Hanoi - Hai Phong expressway makes the trip about 1.5 to 2 hours by car or bus. Trains also run from Hanoi to Hai Phong station in the city centre, a slower but scenic option of about 2.5 hours.

title: Cat Bi Airport
text: Cat Bi International Airport is only about 5 km from the city centre, around 15 to 20 minutes by taxi or ride-hailing car. It has domestic flights to Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang and other cities, plus a few international routes.

title: Tan Vu - Lach Huyen sea bridge
text: Opened in 2017, the Tan Vu - Lach Huyen bridge is one of the longest sea-crossing bridges in Vietnam, at about 5.4 km. It links the city with Cat Hai island and the road to the Cat Ba ferry, and gives wide views over the sea and the deep-water port.

title: Do Son buffalo fighting festival
text: The Do Son buffalo fighting festival is a traditional festival held every year on the 9th day of the 8th lunar month, usually in September. Specially trained buffaloes face each other in an arena in Do Son, and the event draws large crowds, so arrive early.
source: Hai Phong cultural festival information (to verify)
